sentences.zh: 今天，随着艾奥瓦州投票的开始，标志着2020年大选的序幕拉开，我们推出了一档新节目，在11月到来之前报道这个国家和选民。

sentences.zh: 那么，当选可能性这个问题如何影响你是否会投票给伊丽莎白·沃伦？

sentences.en: And they may not for Pete, but some of them will.
sentences.zh: 他们可能不会投给皮特，但其中一些人会。

sentences.en: And some of them will for Warren, I think, too.
sentences.zh: 我想，其中一些人也会投给沃伦。

sentences.en: Just, how many?

sentences.zh: 所以你的部分选票是在琢磨你认为共和党人在大选中会投给谁？

sentences.en: He's down there, maybe, you know.
sentences.zh: 他大概在下面吧，你知道的。

sentences.en: What's the decision there?
sentences.zh: 那里的决定是怎么样的？

sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.zh: 我不认为共和党人会投票给他。

sentences.en: I just, you know, Jesus.

sentences.en: It's much easier going and asking people all these questions than to be making these choices.
sentences.zh: 到处去问别人这些问题，可比做这些选择容易多了。

sentences.en: So, it seems like you're wrestling with it.
sentences.zh: 所以，你似乎在为此纠结。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah, it wasn't that hard last time.
sentences.zh: 对，上次没这么难。

sentences.en: Who'd you caucus for last time?
sentences.zh: 你上次党团会议支持了谁？

sentences.en: We, with Hillary.
sentences.zh: 我们，支持了希拉里。

sentences.en: But, you know, I didn't do something right.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，我有什么事没做好。

sentences.en: Yeah, we did something wrong.
sentences.zh: 对，我们做错了点事。

sentences.en: So, a week before the Iowa caucuses, I went with my colleagues, Austin Mitchell and Andy Mills, to the Des Moines region to talk to voters about how they're feeling.
sentences.zh: 所以，在艾奥瓦州党团会议开始前一周，我和我的同事奥斯汀·米切尔以及安迪·米尔斯一起去了得梅因地区，和选民交流他们的感受。

sentences.en: For months, we've been seeing a really fluid race in the state.
sentences.zh: 几个月来，我们一直看到该州的选情非常多变。

sentences.en: Top candidates like Pete Buttigieg could be leading in one month.
sentences.zh: 像皮特·布蒂吉格这样的领跑候选人可能这个月领先。

sentences.en: Elizabeth Warren could be leading the next.
sentences.zh: 伊丽莎白·沃伦可能下个月领先。

sentences.en: Some polls show Joe Biden leading.
sentences.zh: 一些民调显示乔·拜登领先。

sentences.en: And most recently, Bernie Sanders has held a firm lead at the top.
sentences.zh: 最近，伯尼·桑德斯一直稳居榜首。

sentences.en: Even more, when we started talking to voters, they weren't just deciding between one or two candidates that were the same ideologically,
sentences.zh: 更甚的是，当我们开始与选民交谈时，他们不只是在一两个意识形态相同的候选人之间做决定，

sentences.en: but maybe even between candidates that seemingly have conflicting policy positions.
sentences.zh: 甚至可能在那些政策立场看似冲突的候选人之间摇摆。

sentences.en: So, you can meet a voter who's flipping between Joe Biden and Bernie Sanders.
sentences.zh: 所以，你会遇到一个在乔·拜登和伯尼·桑德斯之间摇摆的选民。

sentences.en: You can meet a voter that's flipping between Elizabeth Warren and Pete Buttigieg.
sentences.zh: 你会遇到一个在伊丽莎白·沃伦和皮特·布蒂吉格之间摇摆的选民。

sentences.en: And so, we wanted to get a better sense of what was going on on the ground.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们想更好地了解实地究竟发生了什么。

sentences.en: We are in the small town of Russell, Iowa.
sentences.zh: 我们来到了艾奥瓦州的小镇拉塞尔。

sentences.en: And over and over, people kept going back to the same moment.
sentences.zh: 人们一次又一次地回到同一个时刻。

sentences.en: Down some very lonely streets to come here and talk to this lady.
sentences.zh: 穿过一些非常荒凉的街道，来这里和这位女士交谈。

sentences.en: Can you guys give me a hand with anything?
sentences.zh: 大家能帮我个忙吗？

sentences.en: We're just out here talking to ourselves.
sentences.zh: 我们只是在自言自语。

sentences.en: Are you Casey?
sentences.zh: 你是凯西吗？

sentences.en: I'm Casey.
sentences.zh: 我是凯西。

sentences.en: I'm Andy.
sentences.zh: 我是安迪。

sentences.en: Andy, nice to meet you.
sentences.zh: 安迪，很高兴认识你。

sentences.en: Hi, Casey.
sentences.zh: 嗨，凯西。

sentences.en: Austin.
sentences.zh: 奥斯汀。

sentences.en: Austin, nice to meet you guys.
sentences.zh: 奥斯汀，很高兴认识你们。

sentences.en: So, a couple days ago, Austin and Andy went out to meet Casey DeHoot.
sentences.zh: 所以，几天前，奥斯汀和安迪去见了凯西·德胡特。

sentences.en: Yeah, my name is Casey DeHoot.
sentences.zh: 对，我叫凯西·德胡特。

sentences.en: I'm 36 years old.
sentences.zh: 我36岁。

sentences.en: I'm a full-time supervisor at a warehouse in the area.
sentences.zh: 我是当地一家仓库的全职主管。

sentences.en: And I am a city councilwoman here in Russell.
sentences.zh: 我还是拉塞尔市的一名市议员。

sentences.en: And for her, and for a lot of Iowa Democrats, the story actually begins in 2008.
sentences.zh: 对她来说，对许多艾奥瓦州的民主党人来说，这个故事实际上始于2008年。

sentences.en: But yeah, I remember that pretty well because it was Obama and it was Hillary.
sentences.zh: 哦对，我对此记忆犹新，因为当时是奥巴马对阵希拉里。

sentences.en: Voters give Clinton high marks for being strong, experienced, decisive, and compassionate.
sentences.zh: 选民对克林顿的评价很高，认为她坚强、有经验、果断且富有同情心。

sentences.en: But is Clinton likable?
sentences.zh: 但克林顿讨人喜欢吗？

sentences.en: And at that time, I don't think Hillary was particularly popular, but she seemed like she was going to be the pretty clear candidate.
sentences.zh: 在当时，我认为希拉里并不是特别受欢迎，但她看起来似乎是胜券在握的候选人。

sentences.en: And then here comes this meteor out of Chicago, which is Barack Obama.
sentences.zh: 然后，来自芝加哥的这颗流星——巴拉克·奥巴马出现了。

sentences.en: The question is whether or not Obama, an African-American candidate from the big city of Chicago, can connect with the primarily white rural voters here.
sentences.zh: 问题在于，奥巴马这个来自芝加哥大都市的非裔候选人，能否与这里主要是白人的农村选民产生共鸣。

sentences.en: I think we're listening.
sentences.zh: 我想我们在倾听。

sentences.en: Thank you, Iowa.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，艾奥瓦。

sentences.en: And then Iowa picked him, and I remember being pretty floored.
sentences.zh: 然后艾奥瓦州选择了她/他，我记得当时震惊不已。

sentences.en: They said, they said this day would never come.
sentences.zh: 他们说，他们说这一天永远不会到来。

sentences.en: But on this January night, at this defining moment in history,
sentences.zh: 但在1月的这个夜晚，在这个具有决定性历史意义的时刻，

sentences.en: you have done what the cynics said we couldn't do.
sentences.zh: 你们做到了那些悲观主义者说我们做不到的事。

sentences.en: Iowa sort of saw the lightning and was able to put it in a bottle.
sentences.zh: 艾奥瓦仿佛捕捉到了那道闪电，并把它装进了瓶子里。

sentences.en: And then the rest of the nation was like, yeah, we see it too.
sentences.zh: 然后全国其他地方的人都觉得，是的，我们也看到了。

sentences.en: You have done what the state of New Hampshire can do in five days.
sentences.zh: 你们完成了新罕布什尔州要在五天内才能做到的事。

sentences.en: You have done what America can do in this new year, 2008.
sentences.zh: 你们完成了美国在这个崭新的2008年所能做到的事。

sentences.en: So 2008 becomes this vitally important year for Iowa Democrats.
sentences.zh: 因此，对艾奥瓦州的民主党人来说，2008年成为至关重要的一年。

sentences.en: They have a sense of pride, a real sense of ownership around Barack Obama's historic campaign.
sentences.zh: 他们对巴拉克·奥巴马具有历史意义的竞选活动有一种自豪感，一种真正的归属感。

sentences.en: They feel like they saw in him what the rest of the country would eventually see, and that they helped launch an upstart candidate to the Democratic nomination,
sentences.zh: 他们觉得自己在他的身上看到了全国其他地方最终会看到的东西，并且他们帮助一位初出茅庐的候选人获得了民主党提名，

sentences.en: and then eventually the historic presidency.
sentences.zh: 并最终开启了具有历史意义的总统任期。

sentences.en: We are one nation.
sentences.zh: 我们是一个国家。

sentences.en: We are one people.
sentences.zh: 我们是一个民族。

sentences.en: And our time for change has come.
sentences.zh: 我们变革的时代已经到来。

sentences.en: But that's not the story of the 2016 campaign, is it?
sentences.zh: 但2016年竞选的故事可不是这样的，对吧？

sentences.en: That was awful.
sentences.zh: 那太糟糕了。

sentences.en: Can we go back to, like, right around this time, about four years ago,
sentences.zh: 我们能回到大约四年前这个时候，

sentences.en: when you were doing this Iowa thing of trying to pick the first candidate?
sentences.zh: 当你正在做艾奥瓦州的这种事情，试图挑选第一位候选人时吗？

sentences.en: The Democrats getting ready for their final face-off tonight in Iowa before voters go out and caucus next week.
sentences.zh: 民主党人正准备今晚在艾奥瓦州进行最后的对决，选民们下周就要去参加党团会议了。

sentences.en: Hillary Clinton, Bernie Sanders, and Martin O'Malley.
sentences.zh: 希拉里·克林顿、伯尼·桑德斯和马丁·奥马利。

sentences.en: Yes, he's still in there.
sentences.zh: 是的，他还待在那里面。

sentences.en: What were you thinking?
sentences.zh: 你当时是怎么想的？

sentences.en: How were you weighing?
sentences.zh: 你是怎么权衡的？

sentences.en: What were you liking?
sentences.zh: 你当时看好谁？

sentences.en: For me, it was pretty obvious early on, Hillary.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，希拉里，早期这其实挺明显的。

sentences.en: But ramping up to the caucus day, Bernie was really starting to gain some steam.
sentences.zh: 但随着党团会议日期的临近，伯尼确实开始积聚起一些声势。

sentences.en: As most polls show, Sanders is closing in on Hillary Clinton's lead in Iowa and beating her in New Hampshire.
sentences.zh: 正如大多数民调显示的那样，桑德斯正在缩小希拉里·克林顿在爱荷华州的领先优势，并在新罕布什尔州击败了她。

sentences.en: And I was like, I could really switch to this guy right now.
sentences.zh: 当时我就想，我此刻真的可以转而支持这个人。

sentences.en: But my only thing about Bernie was Barack Obama had a lot of difficulty getting a lot of legislation through because the different legislative bodies thought he was so liberal
sentences.zh: 但我对伯尼唯一的顾虑是，巴拉克·奥巴马在推动大量立法时遇到了极大的困难，因为不同的立法机构认为他太自由派了

sentences.en: that they didn't really want to do anything with him.
sentences.zh: 以至于他们根本不想和他合作任何事情。

sentences.en: And I thought, well, my God, if Barack Obama can't get that achieved, how are they going to let Bernie Sanders,
sentences.zh: 然后我想，天哪，如果巴拉克·奥巴马都无法达成那些，他们怎么会允许伯尼·桑德斯——

sentences.en: who's this progressive out of, like, nowhere who's asking for all these crazy things?
sentences.zh: 一个不知从哪冒出来的、提出所有这些疯狂要求的激进派——来做这件事呢？

sentences.en: So I thought, nope, it's going to be Hillary.
sentences.zh: 所以我心想，不，还是选希拉里吧。

sentences.en: She's going to be the one who's more electable and a general.
sentences.zh: 她才是那个更有胜算、更有大局观的人。

sentences.en: What happens next is very specific to Iowa's caucus system.
sentences.zh: 接下来发生的事情非常符合爱荷华州党团会议系统的特点。

sentences.en: Rather than a traditional voting booth where someone goes in and selects one candidate,
sentences.zh: 与那种人们走进投票亭选择单一候选人的传统投票方式不同，

sentences.en: caucus goers show up to a big room, oftentimes a gymnasium or a local community center, and they stand in a group with other people who support their candidate.
sentences.zh: 参加党团会议的人们会来到一个大房间里，通常是体育馆或当地社区中心，他们会和支持同一候选人的其他人站在一起。

sentences.en: But that's not a set thing.
sentences.zh: 但这并不是一成不变的。

sentences.en: People can make appeals to each other, and things can shuffle around before the final vote is taken.
sentences.zh: 在最终投票进行之前，人们可以互相游说，场面也可能会重新洗牌。

sentences.en: You know, they asked several times, does anybody want to change their candidate?
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他们问了好几次，有没有人想更换候选人？

sentences.en: This is where everyone's at in the room.
sentences.zh: 这就是房间里每个人目前所处的位置。

sentences.en: Does anybody want to switch sides?
sentences.zh: 有没有人想换阵营？

sentences.en: Last chance.
sentences.zh: 最后一次机会。

sentences.en: And I kept thinking, I could just get up, go over, sit with that other group.
sentences.zh: 但我一直在想，我其实可以站起来，走过去，和那个组坐在一起。

sentences.en: But no, it's going to be Hillary.
sentences.zh: 但转念一想，不行，还是得选希拉里。

sentences.en: Thrilled that I'm coming to New Hampshire after winning Iowa.
sentences.zh: 赢得爱荷华州后，我非常激动能来到新罕布什尔州。

sentences.en: And it was Hillary.
sentences.zh: 结果确实是希拉里。

sentences.en: The first woman ever to win the Iowa caucuses did it by two-tenths of one percent.
sentences.zh: 作为赢得爱荷华州党团会议的第一位女性，她以百分之零点二的微弱优势获胜。

sentences.en: Iowa voted for Clinton over Sanders by the smallest margin in caucus history, 49.8 to 49.6.
sentences.zh: 爱荷华州以党团会议历史上最小的差距将选票投给了克林顿而非桑德斯，比例为49.8%对49.6%。

sentences.en: I thought, well, Hillary's incredibly qualified.
sentences.zh: 我想，好吧，希拉里资历极其深厚。

sentences.en: She's earned it.
sentences.zh: 这是她应得的。

sentences.en: And about nine months later, well, we know what happens.
sentences.zh: 大约九个月后，好吧，大家都知道发生什么了。

sentences.en: Right now, a historic moment.
sentences.zh: 此时此刻，一个历史性的时刻。

sentences.en: We can now project the winner of the presidential race CNN projects.
sentences.zh: CNN现在预测我们可以公布总统竞选的赢家。

sentences.en: Donald Trump wins the presidency.
sentences.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普赢得总统大选。

sentences.en: The business tycoon, a TV personality.
sentences.zh: 这位商业大亨、电视名人。

sentences.en: Capping his improbable political journey with an astounding upset victory.
sentences.zh: 他以一场令人震惊的逆袭胜利，为自己不可思议的政治之旅画上了句号。

sentences.en: Donald J.
sentences.zh: 唐纳德·J·

sentences.en: Trump will become the 45th president of the United States, defeating Hillary Clinton.
sentences.zh: 特朗普将成为美国第45任总统，击败了希拉里·克林顿。

sentences.en: And then once Trump was elected, then I felt like Invasion of the Body Snatchers.
sentences.zh: 然后一旦特朗普当选，我就感觉像是回到了《人体异形侵占》里。

sentences.en: I see all these Trump shirts around, and I'm like, wait, where have I been living?
sentences.zh: 我看到周围到处都是特朗普的衬衫，心想，等等，我到底住在什么地方？

sentences.en: And I was just like, my God, they really hated Hillary.
sentences.zh: 我当时就觉得，天哪，他们是真的很讨厌希拉里。

sentences.en: I really took it as a, you know, less of a Trump win as it was a Hillary loss.
sentences.zh: 我真的觉得与其说这是一场特朗普的胜利，不如说是一场希拉里的失利。

sentences.en: And I feel like they wanted a change in politics.
sentences.zh: 我觉得他们渴望政治变革。

sentences.en: Bernie would have been a change in politics.
sentences.zh: 伯尼本可以带来政治变革。

sentences.en: Hillary Clinton was the status quo.
sentences.zh: 而希拉里·克林顿代表着现状。

sentences.en: They didn't want status quo.
sentences.zh: 他们不想要现状。

sentences.en: And yet you chose her because you found her to be the more reasonable and electable candidate.
sentences.zh: 然而你选择她是因为你发现她是一个更理智、更有胜算的候选人。

sentences.en: Did the election shake that sense, that you knew what was electable?
sentences.zh: 这次选举是否动摇了这种感觉——那种你自以为知道谁更有胜算的感觉？

sentences.en: Very much.
sentences.zh: 很大程度上动摇了。

sentences.en: Very much changed that.
sentences.zh: 很大程度上改变了这一点。

sentences.en: But had I known then, when I know now, I would have switched so faSt.
sentences.zh: 但如果我当时能知道现在所知道的，我早就立马跳槽了。

sentences.en: I would have definitely gone Bernie had I switched and had Bernie been the nominee for the party.
sentences.zh: 如果我早做选择，且伯尼能成为党内提名人，我绝对会选伯尼。

sentences.en: He would be president right now.
sentences.zh: 他现在就是总统了。

sentences.en: Well, when it comes to this year, how confident are you that this time around you can find the candidate that is more electable?
sentences.zh: 那么，说到今年，你有多大信心这次能找到更有胜算的候选人？

sentences.en: Not at all confident.
sentences.zh: 一点信心都没有。

sentences.en: That last election, 2016, was just such a mind blow.
sentences.zh: 上一次2016年的大选实在太震撼了。

sentences.en: I mean, nobody saw that coming.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，谁也没料到会那样。

sentences.en: So, but yeah, so going into this election, you know, that's definitely something that's into my mind is, is what's a candidate that I like and what's a candidate that speaks to me?
sentences.zh: 所以，但是，是的，所以在进入这次大选时，你知道，我心里确实在想，我喜欢什么样的候选人？什么样的候选人能引起我的共鸣？

sentences.en: But what's a candidate that might have a more broad appeal?
sentences.zh: 但什么样的候选人才可能拥有更广泛的吸引力呢？

sentences.en: This is probably the crux of why I'm an undecided caucus goer is because I'm trying to negotiate that space.
sentences.zh: 这可能就是为什么我至今仍是一个摇摆不定的党团会议参与者的核心原因，因为我正在努力在这些矛盾中找到平衡。

sentences.en: So Casey calls it having her mind blown.
sentences.zh: 所以凯西把这称为脑洞大开或深受震撼。

sentences.en: My colleague Alex Burns says that some Democrats feel as if their brains have been broken.
sentences.zh: 我的同事亚历克斯·伯恩斯说，一些民主党人感觉他们的脑子好像被打碎了。

sentences.en: But it's this effect where Democrats do not trust themselves to make the right electoral decision.
sentences.zh: 但这种效应导致民主党人不相信自己能够做出正确的选举决定。

sentences.en: They no longer trust their own instincts about determining what electability is.
sentences.zh: 他们不再相信自己对判断什么是胜算（或竞争力）的直觉。

sentences.en: Do they go with a candidate who speaks to their sense of inspiration, an Obama-like figure, someone who can maybe rally the party through soaring rhetoric or the like?
sentences.zh: 他们是该选择一个能激发他们灵感、像奥巴马一样的人物，一个能通过高超的言辞等方式凝聚党派力量的人？

sentences.en: Or do they try to think of who is most electable to other people, but they don't even know what that is?
sentences.zh: 还是去猜想谁对其他人来说最具胜算——尽管他们甚至不知道那到底是什么？

sentences.en: For a lot of people, they thought that was Hillary Clinton, and that didn't turn out well.
sentences.zh: 对很多人来说，他们曾以为那是希拉里·克林顿，但结果并不好。

sentences.en: And so it just stays to go.
sentences.zh: 所以这依然是个问题。

sentences.en: You're seeing Iowa Democrats really frozen.
sentences.zh: 你可以看到爱荷华州的民主党人真的陷入了迷茫和停滞。

sentences.en: With days until your caucus, while you're still undecided, what is it that you're most afraid of?
sentences.zh: 距离你们的党团会议只有几天了，而你仍然摇摆不定，你内心最害怕的是什么？

sentences.en: That's a good question.
sentences.zh: 这是个好问题。

sentences.en: I'm worried that, you know, the first week in November, you know, that Wednesday after the general election, you know, again, waking up and going, damn it, I did it again.
sentences.zh: 我担心的是，你知道，在十一月的第一周，大选结束后的那个星期三，你知道，又一次醒来然后感叹：该死，我又做了一次。

sentences.en: I voted for the wrong candidate, knowing that I felt better about a different candidate.
sentences.zh: 我明明对另一位候选人感觉更好，却还是投错了候选人。

sentences.en: So we wanted to talk to more undecided voters, like Casey.
sentences.zh: 所以我们想要采访更多像凯西这样摇摆不定的选民。

sentences.en: We are in the Beaverdale neighborhood of Des Moines, Iowa.
sentences.zh: 我们现在在爱荷华州得梅因的比弗代尔社区。

sentences.en: We are walking through this residential neighborhood to knock on some doors and ask Iowans how they're feeling.
sentences.zh: 我们正穿行于这个住宅区，去敲开一些房门，询问爱荷华州民的真实感受。

sentences.en: There's a surprising amount of snow on the ground.
sentences.zh: 地上的积雪多得令人惊讶。

sentences.en: I just hope it doesn't get any colder.
sentences.zh: 我只希望天气别再变冷了。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's a fine line between the strong knock and the police knock, which you don't want to do.
sentences.zh: 对，有力地敲门和像警察查水表一样吓人的敲门之间有一条微妙的界限，后者可千万别做。

sentences.en: Hi, how are you?
sentences.zh: 嗨，你好吗？

sentences.en: My name's Estet.
sentences.zh: 我叫埃斯泰特。

sentences.en: This is Austin and Andy.
sentences.zh: 这位是奥斯汀和安迪。

sentences.en: We're reporters with the New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我们是《纽约时报》的记者。

sentences.en: How's it going?
sentences.zh: 最近怎么样？

sentences.en: Oh, gosh, fine.
sentences.zh: 哦，天哪，挺好的。

sentences.en: I have a sleeping baby, though.
sentences.zh: 不过我有个正在睡觉的婴儿。

sentences.en: Oh, okay.
sentences.zh: 哦，好的。

sentences.en: She just woke up.
sentences.zh: 她刚醒。

sentences.en: Totally fine.
sentences.zh: 完全没关系。

sentences.en: I wonder if we could ask you a couple questions?
sentences.zh: 不知道我们能不能问你几个问题？

sentences.en: I can't.
sentences.zh: 不行。

sentences.en: I'm in the middle of a conference call, actually.
sentences.zh: 其实我正在开电话会议呢。

sentences.en: Sorry.
sentences.zh: 抱歉。

sentences.en: Okay, sorry to interrupt you.
sentences.zh: 好的，打扰了抱歉。

sentences.en: Are you someone who's thought about who you're going to caucus for?
sentences.zh: 你是有考虑过要在党团会议上支持谁的人吗？

sentences.en: Actually, sir, I'm somebody who has to go get his wife.
sentences.zh: 说实话，先生，我现在得去接我太太。

sentences.en: She's getting off at 1 o'clock.
sentences.zh: 她一点钟下班。

sentences.en: Now, you want to report that in the Times.
sentences.zh: 现在，你可得把这事儿报到《纽约时报》上。

sentences.en: I mean, hey, that's big news.
sentences.zh: 我是说，嘿，这可是条大新闻。

sentences.en: Because if I'm not there in time, it'll be big news.
sentences.zh: 因为如果我没及时赶到那儿，这就会变成大新闻。

sentences.en: Oh, okay.
sentences.zh: 哦，好吧。

sentences.en: Obviously, there were some people who were totally decided.
sentences.zh: 显然，有些人是完全已经拿定主意了。

sentences.en: Bernie.
sentences.zh: 伯尼。

sentences.en: No doubts about it.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think we're caucusing for Bernie.
sentences.zh: 对，我想我们会在党团会议上支持伯尼。

sentences.en: Was it a hard choice to pick Bernie?
sentences.zh: 选择伯尼是个艰难的决定吗？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不难。

sentences.en: I'll be caucusing for Bernie Sanders.
sentences.zh: 我将在党团会议上支持伯尼·桑德斯。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Yep.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Are you someone who just made that choice, or this is something that's been true for a long time?
sentences.zh: 你是刚刚才做出这个决定，还是这已经是你长期以来的想法？

sentences.en: Um, it's been true for a long time, uh...
sentences.zh: 嗯，这已经是很久以来的想法了，呃……

sentences.en: Andrew Yang, 2020.
Yeah?
sentences.zh: 是吗？

sentences.en: Yep.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Not undecided.
sentences.zh: 不是摇摆选民。

sentences.en: You know.
sentences.zh: 你知道的。

sentences.en: Yep.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Is there anyone else here that, uh, that is trying to make a decision still that might be willing to chat with us for a bit?
sentences.zh: 这里还有其他人，呃，还在做决定，可能愿意跟我们聊一会儿的吗？

sentences.en: Um, yeah, she likes Joe Biden.
sentences.zh: 嗯，对，她喜欢乔·拜登。

sentences.en: Damn!
sentences.zh: 该死！

sentences.en: Are you going to caucus for Joe Biden?
sentences.zh: 你要在党团会议上支持乔·拜登吗？

sentences.en: No, I'm going to caucus for Pete Buttigieg.
sentences.zh: 不，我要支持皮特·布蒂吉格。

sentences.en: Pete Buttigieg.
sentences.zh: 皮特·布蒂吉格。

sentences.en: Can we chat with her for just a little bit?
sentences.zh: 我们能跟她聊一小会儿吗？

sentences.en: She says she's too hungover.
sentences.zh: 她说她宿醉太严重了。

sentences.en: Hungover roommate.
sentences.zh: 宿醉的室友。

sentences.en: Do you want to share your thoughts on your candidate?
sentences.zh: 你想分享一下你对你支持的候选人的看法吗？

sentences.en: Do you want to share your political opinions?
sentences.zh: 你想分享你的政治观点吗？

sentences.en: No, I want to vomit.
sentences.zh: 不想，我想吐。

sentences.en: See, hangover people vote for Pete Buttigieg.
sentences.zh: 你看，宿醉的人都投票给皮特·布蒂吉格。

sentences.en: I'm clear-minded, though, so that's why I'm for Ying.
sentences.zh: 不过我头脑很清醒，所以我才支持杨。

sentences.en: But just as often.
sentences.zh: 但同样经常发生的是。

sentences.en: Hi.
sentences.zh: 嗨。

sentences.en: Hey, I'm sorry.
sentences.zh: 嘿，对不起。

sentences.en: I thought you were somebody else.
sentences.zh: 我以为你是别人。

sentences.en: I don't have time.
sentences.zh: 我没时间。

sentences.en: All right, bye-bye.
sentences.zh: 好吧，拜拜。

sentences.en: We're just, uh, we're just reporters just trying to gauge the, uh, the caucus on Monday.
sentences.zh: 我们只是，呃，我们只是记者，想了解一下周一党团会议的情况。

sentences.en: Are you planning on going?
sentences.zh: 你们打算去吗？

sentences.en: Yes, I thought you were selling something.
sentences.zh: 去，我还以为你们是来推销什么的。

sentences.en: Okay, I'm on my way out.
sentences.zh: 好的，我正要出门。

sentences.en: But, honestly, um, I can't decide.
sentences.zh: 但是，说实话，嗯，我拿不定主意。

sentences.en: I don't, I'm not a Bernie lover, so if you guys are Bernie bros, I like,
sentences.zh: 我不，我不是伯尼的狂热粉丝，所以如果你们是伯尼的拥趸，我觉得——

sentences.en: okay, so then it's sort of like, I want to vote for, I want to vote for someone who people in Michigan,
sentences.zh: 好吧，所以这就有点像，我想投票给，我想投票给一个密歇根州、

sentences.en: Ohio, and Pennsylvania will vote for.
sentences.zh: 俄亥俄州和宾夕法尼亚州的人会投票的候选人。

sentences.en: That's who I want to vote for.
sentences.zh: 那才是我想要投票的人。

sentences.en: And do you have, is there anybody in the front of mind that you think is best for that?
sentences.zh: 你心里有没有觉得谁最适合这个标准？

sentences.en: Elizabeth, and I love Amy.
sentences.zh: 伊丽莎白，而且我很喜欢埃米。

sentences.en: I mean, I'd really like to vote for a woman, because, you know, I'm going to die soon, and there's not, still not been a woman president.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我真的很想投给一位女性，因为，你知道的，我快要死了，而且还没有，至今还没有出现过女总统。

sentences.en: But I feel like there's so much prejudice against us Bettys, you know what I mean?
sentences.zh: 但我觉得我们这些女性受到的偏见太重了，你知道我的意思吗？

sentences.en: I've got to think about it in bigger terms than who I was.
sentences.zh: 我得从比我自身更宏大的角度来思考。

sentences.en: I'm kind of obsessive about politics.
sentences.zh: 我对政治有点着迷。

sentences.en: I know, I can hear the TV out in the background.
sentences.zh: 我知道，我能听到背景里放着电视声音。

sentences.en: Well, it's got to be loud enough, but I'm getting ready.
sentences.zh: 嗯，声音得开大点，不过我正在准备。

sentences.en: Have you made a decision on who you're going to caucus for?
sentences.zh: 你决定好党内预选要支持谁了吗？

sentences.en: I have it down to two.
sentences.zh: 我精简到了两个人。

sentences.en: The two I came down to are the one I support the most, and the one I think probably has the best chance to win.
sentences.zh: 我最后留下的两个人，一个是我最支持的，另一个是我认为最有希望获胜的。

sentences.en: So I think I'm going to caucus, I think, for Amy Klobuchar.
sentences.zh: 所以我想我预选大概会支持埃米·克洛布查尔。

sentences.en: And then I imagine she's not going to have enough.
sentences.zh: 然后我想她可能票数不够。

sentences.en: So then I think I'll probably go to Joe Biden.
sentences.zh: 所以我想我最后可能会转投乔·拜登。

sentences.en: Yeah, what was that like for you?
sentences.zh: 是啊，那对你来说是什么样的体验？

sentences.en: Yeah, well, it felt like I'd love to go with just a gut feeling.
sentences.zh: 对，感觉我其实很想完全凭直觉走。

sentences.en: I love somebody really a lot, but I don't have that person so much this year, like when Obama was around, you know.
sentences.zh: 我很喜欢某个人，但今年我没有那种强烈的赶脚，不像当年奥巴马在的时候，你知道的。

sentences.en: That was really nice to have that gut feeling.
sentences.zh: 那种全凭直觉的感觉真的很棒。

sentences.en: So you'd have to just do it more intellectually, gather more information, the more you can get, the more wise decision you can make, and go from there.
sentences.zh: 所以你得更理性地对待，收集更多信息，掌握的信息越多，就能做出越明智的决定，然后顺其自然。

sentences.en: Does that answer your question?
sentences.zh: 这回答你的问题了吗？

sentences.en: But with that intellectual decision, it seems it's not just a personal intellectual decision.
sentences.zh: 但带着这种理性决策，似乎这不仅是个人的理性决定。

sentences.en: You're trying to project a little bit into the minds of others.
sentences.zh: 你还得试着去揣测其他人的想法。

sentences.en: When it comes down to the who I think can win part, definitely.
sentences.zh: 说到谁能赢这一点，绝对是这样的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: And how have you been factoring that?
sentences.zh: 你是怎么把这一点考虑进去的？

sentences.en: I'm hearing a lot of people that don't think anybody but Biden can really win.
sentences.zh: 我听到很多人觉得除了拜登没人能真正赢得大选。

sentences.en: I'm not sure I totally agree with that, but I think this year's election is special because we need to make sure that we win.
sentences.zh: 我不敢说我完全同意这一点，但我认为今年的选举很特殊，因为我们必须确保获胜。

sentences.en: And about everybody I talk to, the main focus is making sure Trump doesn't have another four years.
sentences.zh: 而且我交谈过的大多数人，核心焦点都是确保特朗普不能再干四年。

sentences.en: And it's not so much get that candidate you love, it's get him out.
sentences.zh: 与其说选出你深爱的候选人，不如说要把他赶下台。

sentences.en: We are finding a few people.
sentences.zh: 我们确实发现了一些人。

sentences.en: Everyone seems to be pretty nice.
sentences.zh: 每个人看起来都挺友善的。

sentences.en: You guys look like you're leaving, though.
sentences.zh: 不过你们看起来要走了。

sentences.en: Can we just ask you two questions?
sentences.zh: 我们能问你们两个问题吗？

sentences.en: Are you planning on voting next week?
sentences.zh: 你们打算下周投票吗？

sentences.en: Who's your number one?
sentences.zh: 谁是你们的首选？

sentences.en: Who's your number one?
sentences.zh: 谁是你们的首选？

sentences.en: I don't know yet.
sentences.zh: 我还不知道。

sentences.en: You don't know?
sentences.zh: 你不知道？

sentences.en: That's why we want to ask you about it.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我们想问问你们。

sentences.en: When do you think you'll make your decision?
sentences.zh: 你觉得你什么时候能做决定？

sentences.en: Probably there.
sentences.zh: 大概就在那会儿吧。

sentences.en: Probably there?
sentences.zh: 大概在那会儿？

sentences.en: Why is it so hard?
sentences.zh: 为什么这么难决定？

sentences.en: It's all about electability, so it's hard to decide what factors are going to control electability.
sentences.zh: 这全关乎当选胜算，所以很难决定究竟哪些因素会左右胜算。

sentences.en: So it's complicated.
sentences.zh: 所以这很复杂。

sentences.en: You just want to win in November?
sentences.zh: 你们只是想在十一月赢吗？

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: You guys are fucking idiots.
sentences.zh: 你们这群白痴。

sentences.en: Six months ago, the Democratic primary was all about the ideological divides.
sentences.zh: 六个月前，民主党初选还全都是关于意识形态的分歧。

sentences.en: There were the progressives, who were promising systemic change and upheaval.
sentences.zh: 有承诺带来系统性变革和剧变的进步派。

sentences.en: And the moderates, who wanted to work more within the system.
sentences.zh: 还有希望在体制内进行改良的温和派。

sentences.en: But now, it's just about who can win.
sentences.zh: 但现在，一切都只取决于谁能赢。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》App？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 解锁了？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 大家都知道，你需要订阅《纽约时报》才能阅读所有报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore the Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果能免费体验《纽约时报》一个月，还不需要绑定信用卡呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在可以了。

sentences.en: When you download the New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你首次下载《纽约时报》App时，你的第一个月应用体验是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 有一个月的时间突破付费墙，看看时报订阅者每天都能读到什么。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅《纽约时报》，今天就下载时报App，享受30天免费阅读权限。

sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.zh: 你们有时间聊聊吗？

sentences.en: Oh, hi, I'm Pat Bode.
sentences.zh: 哦，你好，我是帕特·博德。

sentences.en: Hi, Pat.
sentences.zh: 你好，帕特。

sentences.en: I'm Andy.
sentences.zh: 我是安迪。

sentences.en: Hi, Andy.
sentences.zh: 你好，安迪。

sentences.en: Austin.
sentences.zh: 奥斯汀。

sentences.en: Austin.
sentences.zh: 奥斯汀。

sentences.en: Nice to meet you.
sentences.zh: 很高兴认识你们。

sentences.en: And you guys are...
sentences.zh: 你们是……

sentences.en: So after a day of knocking on doors, a very cold day of knocking on doors, we decided to go to a coffee shop nearby.
sentences.zh: 所以在敲了一天门、非常寒冷的一天挨家挨户敲门之后，我们决定去附近的咖啡馆。

sentences.en: And we found Pat sitting at a table.
sentences.zh: 然后我们发现帕特正坐在桌子旁。

sentences.en: I think what people do not necessarily appreciate, unless they've spent some time here, is just how seriously we take this job.
sentences.zh: 我认为人们未必能体谅到的一点是，除非他们在这里待过一段时间，那就是我们对这份工作有多么认真。

sentences.en: I have several friends.
sentences.zh: 我有好几个朋友。

sentences.en: We've all tried to make sure we've seen pretty much every candidate in person.
sentences.zh: 我们都努力确保见过几乎每一位候选人本人。

sentences.en: And how many people involved with the different campaigns do you think you've spoken to?
sentences.zh: 你觉得你和不同竞选团队的相关人员交流过多少次？

sentences.en: Oh, I've spoken to almost all of the candidates.
sentences.zh: 哦，我和几乎所有的候选人都交流过。

sentences.en: I may have missed Marianne Williamson, but I think I have spoken to every other candidate in the field.
sentences.zh: 我可能漏掉了玛丽安·威廉姆森，但我想我跟场上的其他每位候选人都聊过。

sentences.en: I don't think I'm alone in that.
sentences.zh: 我想我并不是唯一一个这样做的人。

sentences.en: When you say spoken to, do you mean like we are speaking right now?
sentences.zh: 当你说的“交流过”，是指像我们现在这样说话吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I've probably been to a total of 20 plus or more events.
sentences.zh: 我大概参加过总共20多场甚至更多的活动。

sentences.en: And some of them have been long-form conversations.
sentences.zh: 其中有些还是深度长谈。

sentences.en: There was a Steyer event at a friend's house just the other day.
sentences.zh: 前几天在朋友家刚举办了一场斯泰尔的活动。

sentences.en: I saw Elizabeth Warren at our representative's pharmacy.
sentences.zh: 我在我们代表的药店见到了伊丽莎白·沃伦。

sentences.en: There were like 10 of us there and Elizabeth Warren.
sentences.zh: 当时那里大概有10个人和伊丽莎白·沃伦。

sentences.en: And I mean, I'm telling you, you just, you feel like you get to know him quite a little bit.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我跟你说，你真的会觉得对他/她有相当多的了解。

sentences.en: Did that help answer your question?
sentences.zh: 这帮到你回答问题了吗？

sentences.en: That was delightful.
sentences.zh: 这太棒了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: So believe it or not, Pat's process is pretty typical of the Iowa caucus goer.
sentences.zh: 所以信不信由你，帕特的这一套流程在爱荷华州党团会议选民中相当具有代表性。

sentences.en: They take real pride in meeting multiple presidential candidates and vetting them and asking them tough questions.
sentences.zh: 他们为能见到多位总统候选人、对他们进行背景审查并向他们提出尖锐问题而感到真正的自豪。

sentences.en: And they see it as their personal duty because they're the state that votes first in the primaries.
sentences.zh: 他们认为这是自己的个人责任，因为他们是在初选中首个投票的州。

sentences.en: And like a lot of other Iowa Democrats this year, Pat's making this decision on the basis of who's best positioned to beat President Trump.
sentences.zh: 和今年许多其他爱荷华州的民主党人一样，帕特也是基于谁最有实力击败特朗普总统来做这个决定的。

sentences.en: And she was struggling with.
sentences.zh: 而她一直在纠结的是。

sentences.en: Who were the candidates that you were really fighting between in your mind?
sentences.zh: 在你心中，你真正在几个候选人之间纠结的是谁？

sentences.en: Warren, Booker, Buttigieg.
sentences.zh: 沃伦、布克、布蒂吉格。

sentences.en: And then, of course, Steyer came into the picture.
sentences.zh: 然后，当然，斯泰尔也进入了视野。

sentences.en: Quite frankly, the vast majority of the field was really appealing.
sentences.zh: 坦率地说，绝大多数候选人都极具吸引力。

sentences.en: But at a certain point, she just changed the way she was thinking.
sentences.zh: 但在某个时刻，她的思维方式改变了。

sentences.en: I think a lot of us were thinking about electability for a long time.
sentences.zh: 我想我们很多人很长一段时间都在考虑当选胜算。

sentences.en: And I finally realized I don't have the expertise to pick electability.
sentences.zh: 我终于意识到我没有挑选胜算的专业眼光。

sentences.en: It's hard.
sentences.zh: 这太难了。

sentences.en: I mean, you can't even try.
sentences.zh: 我是说，你甚至无法去尝试。

sentences.en: The polls are messy.
sentences.zh: 民调乱成一团。

sentences.en: You know, the electoral college is in the mix.
sentences.zh: 你知道，选举人团制度也搅在里面。

sentences.en: It's just a very difficult choice to make that way.
sentences.zh: 用这种方式做出选择实在是太难了。

sentences.en: So I'm going to pick on the basis of who do I think would make a great president.
sentences.zh: 所以我要根据谁能成为一位伟大的总统来做选择。

sentences.en: And when she did that, her choice became pretty clear.
sentences.zh: 当她这样做时，她的选择变得相当明朗。

sentences.en: Mayor Pete Buttigieg.
sentences.zh: 市长皮特·布蒂吉格。

sentences.en: I was really looking for someone that was a combination of climate and character and the ability to unify the country.
sentences.zh: 我真正在寻找的是兼具气候观、品格以及团结国家能力的人。

sentences.en: So when I put all of those pieces together, that added up to Pete Buttigieg.
sentences.zh: 所以当我把所有这些拼图凑在一起时，指向的就是皮特·布蒂吉格。

sentences.en: So where are we right now?
sentences.zh: 所以我们现在在哪儿？

sentences.en: What is this?
sentences.zh: 这是什么地方？

sentences.en: We are at the Urbandale field office for Pete for America, about to attend the last precinct training for Pete's precinct captains in Urbandale.
sentences.zh: 我们身处厄班代尔的“皮特为了美国”竞选办公室，即将参加厄班代尔皮特团队 precinct 队长们的最后一次基层培训。

sentences.en: Oh, cool.
sentences.zh: 哦，酷。

sentences.en: And there's Pete signs up everywhere.
sentences.zh: 到处都是皮特的标语。

sentences.en: We've got some coffee and crackers.
sentences.zh: 我们准备了咖啡和饼干。

sentences.en: People set on me.
sentences.zh: 人们坐在我周围。

sentences.en: So we wanted to spend time with the Buttigieg campaign, because it's notable that here in Iowa, he's doing significantly better than he's doing in other parts of the country.
sentences.zh: 所以我们想花时间跟布蒂吉格的竞选团队在一起，因为值得注意的是，在这里的爱荷华州，他的表现明显好于他在全国其他地区的表现。

sentences.en: And part of the reason that's been true is that voters here see him as an Obama-analogous figure.
sentences.zh: 部分原因在于这里的选民将他视为奥巴马式的人物。

sentences.en: They see another young Midwesterner, someone who would be a historic president as the first openly gay president,
sentences.zh: 他们看到了另一位年轻的中西部人，一个作为首位公开同性恋身份的总统而载入史册的人，

sentences.en: and also someone who speaks their rhetorical language about inspiration, about coming together, about knitting the country's moral fabric back together.
sentences.zh: 同时也是一个使用他们的修辞语言来谈论激励、谈论凝聚、谈论重塑国家道德纽带的人。

sentences.en: And his campaign has been hearing the same things about electability that we've been hearing.
sentences.zh: 他的竞选团队也听到了我们一直在听到的关于当选胜算的言论。

sentences.en: And so to close the deal in Iowa, they're making an argument to try to get more Iowans to think like Pat,
sentences.zh: 因此，为了在爱荷华州锁定胜局，他们正在提出一个论点，试图让更多的爱荷华人像帕特一样思考，

sentences.en: to embrace the idea that the most electable candidate is the one that inspires you the moSt.
sentences.zh: 去接受这样一种观念：最有胜算的候选人就是那个最能激励你的人。

sentences.en: His intellect drew me firSt.
sentences.zh: 他的才华首先吸引了我。

sentences.en: You know, that was the first thing.
sentences.zh: 你知道，那是第一点。

sentences.en: I thought, you know, there's no doubt.
sentences.zh: 我想，你知道的，这毫无疑问。

sentences.en: And the more I looked at him, goodness, he speaks several languages.
sentences.zh: 而且我越关注他，天哪，他会说好几种语言。

sentences.en: He's a vet.
sentences.zh: 他是个退伍军人。

sentences.en: He's everything you could possibly want.
sentences.zh: 他具备你所能想要的一切。

sentences.en: Him being a veteran is one of the keys for me.
sentences.zh: 他是退伍军人这一点对我来说是关键之一。

sentences.en: He knows what it's like to be on the receiving end of those deployment orders.
sentences.zh: 他深知接到那些部署命令并成为执行对象的感受。

sentences.en: I was really impressed with him.
sentences.zh: 我对他的印象非常深刻。

sentences.en: He was very intelligent, very straightforward.
sentences.zh: 他非常聪明，非常坦率。

sentences.en: I like the fact that he's young.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢他年轻这一点。

sentences.en: I mean, I'm just, I'm tired of old white men.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我只是，我厌倦了老白男。

sentences.en: I'm sorry, Jim.
sentences.zh: 对不起，吉姆。

sentences.en: What do you mean that?
sentences.zh: 你这话是什么意思？

sentences.en: Wait a minute.
sentences.zh: 等一下。

sentences.en: Let me rephrase that.
sentences.zh: 让我重新组织一下语言。

sentences.en: There are none here.
sentences.zh: 这里没有那种人。

sentences.en: And I wanted to listen to somebody with some new ideas, with some ideas of middle American values, and that's why I picked him.
sentences.zh: 我想听听带有新思想的人、带有美国中部价值观思想的人讲话，这就是我选择他的原因。

sentences.en: I'd love to see Pete on a debate stage with Trump.
sentences.zh: 我很想看到皮特和特朗普同台辩论。

sentences.en: Oh, yeah.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的。

sentences.en: Oh, yeah.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的。

sentences.en: Oh, my gosh.
sentences.zh: 噢，天哪。

sentences.en: Oh, my gosh.
sentences.zh: 噢，天哪。

sentences.en: I'd pay good money for that.
sentences.zh: 我愿意花大价钱看这个。

sentences.en: I'd dip into my savings, even.
sentences.zh: 甚至动用我的积蓄我都愿意。

sentences.en: Five points so you can hear me.
sentences.zh: 伸出五指，如果能听到我说话。

sentences.en: Clap twice if you can hear me.
sentences.zh: 如果能听到我说话，就拍手两次。

sentences.en: Great.
sentences.zh: 很好。

sentences.en: Must be at leaSt.
sentences.zh: 至少得……

sentences.en: Oh, look at this group.
sentences.zh: 哦，看看这群人。

sentences.en: We've got a good group in here.
sentences.zh: 我们这里有一群很棒的人。

sentences.en: Hey.
sentences.zh: 嘿。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 对，对。

sentences.en: Yes, Pete.
sentences.zh: 好的，皮特。

sentences.en: I really appreciate everyone coming.
sentences.zh: 我真的很感激大家的到来。

sentences.en: We're all here for one reason, and that's because we believe Pete is the candidate that we need right now.
sentences.zh: 我们来到这里只有一个原因，那就是我们相信皮特正是我们现在需要的候选人。

sentences.en: And you know what Pete needs?
sentences.zh: 你们知道皮特需要什么吗？

sentences.en: Us.
sentences.zh: 我们。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: You guys are a smart group of people.
sentences.zh: 你们是一群聪明的人。

sentences.en: I'm done.
sentences.zh: 我说完了。

sentences.en: You guys got it.
sentences.zh: 你们都懂的。

sentences.en: We've been around the bar.
sentences.zh: 我们酒吧都去过了。

sentences.en: You've been around the bar a few times.
sentences.zh: 你这酒吧也去过好几次了。

sentences.en: People will be sold on Pete.
sentences.zh: 大家会被皮特吸引的。

sentences.en: They just need to hear his message.
sentences.zh: 他们只是需要听到他的诉求。

sentences.en: And when you finally get someone to talk to, and you can convey that message to them, they become a believer.
sentences.zh: 当你终于有机会和某人交谈，并把这个信息传达给他们时，他们就会成为信徒。

sentences.en: They become a supporter, and they will join our team.
sentences.zh: 他们会成为支持者，并加入我们的团队。

sentences.en: We have only a few days left.
sentences.zh: 我们只剩下几天时间了。

sentences.en: We are running out of time right now.
sentences.zh: 我们现在时间不多了。

sentences.en: This is your last chance to show Iowa, to show the country, that Pete can have a strong showing.
sentences.zh: 这是你们向爱荷华州、向全国展示皮特能够有强劲表现的最后机会。

sentences.en: Pete can come through.
sentences.zh: 皮特一定能行。

sentences.en: If you don't understand this urgency right now, you haven't been following the news.
sentences.zh: 如果你现在还不明白这种紧迫感，说明你根本没关注新闻。

sentences.en: We have a few days left, guys.
sentences.zh: 我们只剩下几天了，伙计们。

sentences.en: So turn to your neighbor, tell them I'm excited to be coming and door knocking.
sentences.zh: 所以，转过身对身边的邻居说，我很高兴能来敲门拜访。

sentences.en: Go ahead.
sentences.zh: 去吧。

sentences.en: Do that right now.
sentences.zh: 现在就做。

sentences.en: So, can you tell me your name?
sentences.zh: 那么，能告诉我你的名字吗？

sentences.en: Julie Widoff.
sentences.zh: 朱莉·维多夫。

sentences.en: And what do you do?
sentences.zh: 你以前是做什么的？

sentences.en: I'm retired.
sentences.zh: 我退休了。

sentences.en: I was a financial planner for 40 years.
sentences.zh: 我当了40年财务规划师。

sentences.en: So, Julie's one of the volunteers at the event, and she's been personally inspired by Buttigieg.
sentences.zh: 所以，朱莉是这次活动的志愿者之一，她一直深受布蒂吉格的鼓舞。

sentences.en: I heard him for the first time on a broadcast with Preet Bharara.
sentences.zh: 我第一次听到他的声音是在普里特·巴拉拉的广播节目里。

sentences.en: And I was driving in my car, and I tuned in about five minutes after it started, and I had no idea who he was.
sentences.zh: 当时我正开着车，节目开始大约五分钟后我才调到那个台，我根本不知道他是谁。

sentences.en: And I listened for the remaining 40 minutes of the broadcast, and I remember sitting in my driveway thinking, like, gosh, who is this guy?
sentences.zh: 我听完了节目剩下的40分钟，我记得自己坐在车道上想，天哪，这家伙是谁？

sentences.en: He is so smart.
sentences.zh: 他太聪明了。

sentences.en: He was answering multiple-point questions, you know, just so articulately.
sentences.zh: 他在回答那些多重问题时，你知道，表达得如此清晰流利。

sentences.en: So, I canvas most weekends.
sentences.zh: 所以，我大部分周末都在拉票。

sentences.en: I have for the last couple of months.
sentences.zh: 过去几个月我一直都在这么做。

sentences.en: So, I've knocked on about 400 doors.
sentences.zh: 所以，我已经敲了大约400扇门了。

sentences.en: I'll probably hit 500 by the end of this weekend.
sentences.zh: 到这个周末结束时，我大概能敲到500扇。

sentences.en: And when you knock on doors, what's the issues that come up the most often?
sentences.zh: 当你挨家挨户敲门时，最常出现的问题是什么？

sentences.en: How to beat President Trump.
sentences.zh: 如何击败特朗普总统。

sentences.en: As a group, Democrats are so traumatized by the entire Trump experience that we're kind of like a group of deer in the headlights.
sentences.zh: 作为一个群体，民主党人被整个特朗普时期的经历创伤得太深了，以至于我们就像一群面对车灯不知所措的鹿。

sentences.en: So, the bottom line of conversation always comes around, too.
sentences.zh: 所以，谈话的核心最终总是会绕回到……

sentences.en: You know, I'll support anybody in the field.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我支持候选人名单里的任何人。

sentences.en: I like this person, or I like that person.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢这个人，或者我喜欢那个人。

sentences.en: But so often, I'll hear, well, Pete's in my top three, but I like so-and-so, and maybe it needs to be Joe Biden, because maybe he's the most electable.
sentences.zh: 但很多时候我会听到，嗯，皮特排在我的前三名，但我喜欢某某某，也许应该选乔·拜登，因为他可能是最有胜算的。

sentences.en: So, the conversation just goes around and around.
sentences.zh: 所以，谈话就这样转来转去。

sentences.en: And then, we just talk about, or I talk about the things that draw me to Pete.
sentences.zh: 然后，我们就会讨论，或者我就会谈谈吸引我支持皮特的那些特质。

sentences.en: When I listen to him speak, my blood pressure goes down instead of up.
sentences.zh: 当我听他讲话时，我的血压不仅没有升高，反而下降了。

sentences.en: I'm tired of the politics of outrage.
sentences.zh: 我厌倦了愤怒政治。

sentences.en: I'm tired of being outraged.
sentences.zh: 我厌倦了感到愤怒。

sentences.en: Does, speaking of politics of outrage, I mean, I think about Bernie Sanders.
sentences.zh: 说到愤怒政治，我的意思是，我想到了伯尼·桑德斯。

sentences.en: Would you, would the prospect of a Sanders nomination as a Democrat make you nervous?
sentences.zh: 你会不会，桑德斯作为民主党候选人参选的前景会让你感到紧张吗？

sentences.en: Yes, because I personally don't think he's electable.
sentences.zh: 是的，因为我个人认为他没有胜算。

sentences.en: I don't think that his extreme left-wing policies will garner the support he needs, particularly in the electoral college states that we need to win.
sentences.zh: 我认为他那极左的政策无法获得他所需要的支持，特别是在我们必须赢下的选举人团州。

sentences.en: So, on those levels, it concerns me.
sentences.zh: 所以，从这些层面来看，这让我担忧。

sentences.en: I don't personally have a strong feeling one way or the other about Bernie.
sentences.zh: 我个人对伯尼本身没有太强烈的好恶倾向。

sentences.en: It's just a fear of looking at his politics, having a life of experience, watching how this country functions, and feeling that if the country as a majority
sentences.zh: 这只是一种担忧：审视他的政治主张，结合自己一生的经验，观察这个国家的运作方式，然后觉得如果这个国家的大多数人

sentences.en: wanted a Democratic Socialist government, the Congress would be full of Democratic Socialists.
sentences.zh: 想要一个民主社会主义政府，国会就会充满民主社会主义者。

sentences.en: We would be electing those people, and we don't.
sentences.zh: 我们就会选出这样的人，但我们并没有。

sentences.en: So, sure, it's a concern.
sentences.zh: 所以，当然，这是一个隐忧。

sentences.en: I asked Julie this because of another dynamic that's happening among Democrats.
sentences.zh: 我问朱莉这个问题是因为民主党内部正在发生的另一种动态。

sentences.en: So, Sanders is also pulling ahead in New Hampshire, the second state to vote after Iowa.
sentences.zh: 所以，桑德斯在继爱荷华之后的第二个投票州新罕布什尔州也正在领先。

sentences.en: And so, one of the problems that all this indecision is causing for the other campaigns is that a clear rival to Sanders is yet to emerge in the first two states.
sentences.zh: 因此，所有这些优柔寡断给其他竞选团队带来的问题之一是，在头两个州中，尚未出现一个能够明显抗衡桑德斯的劲敌。

sentences.en: Their support is fractured.
sentences.zh: 他们的支持率四分五裂。

sentences.en: And no candidate has won both Iowa and New Hampshire and then gone on to lose the Democratic nomination.
sentences.zh: 而且还没有哪个候选人既赢了爱荷华又赢了新罕布什尔，最后却输掉了民主党提名。

sentences.en: Doesn't that mean, though, that the Biden, Buttigieg, Klobuchar wing needs to pick a person and stick with it?
sentences.zh: 难道这不意味着，拜登、布蒂吉格、克洛布查这一派需要选定一个人并坚定支持吗？

sentences.en: We'll get there.
sentences.zh: 我们会走到那一步的。

sentences.en: Yeah, we're early in the process.
sentences.zh: 对，我们还在初选的早期阶段。

sentences.en: You know, the electability issue, to me, I guess my main feeling is that knowing our history as Democrats,
sentences.zh: 你知道，胜算问题，对我来说，我想我主要的感受是，回顾我们民主党人的历史，

sentences.en: in the last 60 years, we've won when we've nominated somebody that's young, inspirational, outside the Washington politics.
sentences.zh: 在过去的60年里，每当我们提名年轻、富有号召力、体制外的候选人时，我们就能赢得大选。

sentences.en: When we try and go with somebody that's safe and electable, we lose.
sentences.zh: 当我们试图选择那些稳妥且看似有胜算的人时，我们就会失败。

sentences.en: And I just, I do feel that Pete can put together that coalition.
sentences.zh: 我真的觉得皮特能够凝聚起这样一个联盟。

sentences.en: So, Julie's essentially bringing us back to where we started.
sentences.zh: 所以，朱莉本质上把我们带回了起点。

sentences.en: To 2008, when Iowa captured that lightning in a bottle and helped spring Barack Obama to the Democratic nomination.
sentences.zh: 带回了2008年，当时爱荷华州捕捉到了那种神奇的机遇，帮助巴拉克·奥巴马冲向了民主党提名。

sentences.en: And with that logic, 2016 is the aberration.
sentences.zh: 按照这个逻辑，2016年只是个特例。

sentences.en: And Democrats shouldn't use that fear of electability as a framework for choosing candidates going forward.
sentences.zh: 民主党人不应该把对胜算的恐惧作为未来挑选候选人的框架。

sentences.en: My personal belief is that anyone who has any faith in their powers of political prognostication after 2016 is either delusional or much more plugged in than I am.
sentences.zh: 我个人的看法是，在2016年之后，任何对自己的政治预测能力抱有信心的人，要么是在妄想，要么就比我消息灵通得多。

sentences.en: One of the two.
sentences.zh: 必居其一。

sentences.en: Maybe both.
sentences.zh: 也许两者兼有。

sentences.en: This is Jay, another Buttigieg volunteer.
sentences.zh: 这是杰伊，另一位布蒂吉格的志愿者。

sentences.en: Well, so, I think that most Iowans do know our outsized import in the sense that if a candidate does well here, it's a launching pad.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以，我认为大多数爱荷华州人都知道我们有着举足轻重的影响力，因为如果一个候选人在这里表现良好，这就是一个发射台。

sentences.en: Generally, you get that big bounce in the polls.
sentences.zh: 通常，你会获得民调的大幅反弹。

sentences.en: You're going to have a, you know, position to do better in New Hampshire, Nevada, South Carolina.
sentences.zh: 你就会处于一个有利的位置，你知道的，能在新罕布什尔州、内华达州、南卡罗来纳州做得更好。

sentences.en: And if you can show, like Barack Obama did, that you can win over Iowans, you know, the rest of the country pays attention to that.
sentences.zh: 如果你能像巴拉克·奥巴马那样证明自己能赢得爱荷华州人的支持，你知道的，全国其他地方就会对此予以关注。

sentences.en: We do, I think some Iowans do get in a little chicken and the egg.
sentences.zh: 我们确实，我认为有些爱荷华州人确实陷入了一种鸡生蛋还是蛋生鸡的困境。

sentences.en: So, it's like we look at the rest of the country and we go, who's doing well there?
sentences.zh: 所以这就好比我们看着全国其他地方然后问，谁在那儿表现好？

sentences.en: Because I want somebody who can win across the country.
sentences.zh: 因为我想要一个能在全国各地赢得胜利的人。

sentences.en: And then the rest of the country is kind of looking at us.
sentences.zh: 然后全国其他地方又反过来看着我们。

sentences.en: It's like, all right, well, who can do well in middle America, right?
sentences.zh: 这就好像是，好吧，那谁能在美国腹地表现好呢，对吧？

sentences.en: And so, there is this sort of feedback loop that we can get caught in.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们确实会陷入这种某种程度上的反馈循环中。

sentences.en: And there's just no, like, off-ramp, which is why, for me, it just makes a ton more sense to support the candidate that excites you
sentences.zh: 而且根本没有出口，这就是为什么对我来说，支持那个让你兴奋的候选人在逻辑上要合理得多，

sentences.en: and trust that the things that are exciting to you are exciting to your neighbors and people around the country as well.
sentences.zh: 并且坚信那些让你兴奋的事情同样也会让你的邻居和全国各地的人感到兴奋。

sentences.en: So, you're saying you're trying not to play the electability game, but that your most important issue is winning in November.
sentences.zh: 所以你是说，你尽量不玩胜算游戏，但你最关心的问题是在十一月赢得大选。

sentences.en: All of my most important issues flow from winning in November, right?
sentences.zh: 我所有最核心的关切都源于十一月的胜利，对吧？

sentences.en: So, in that regard, sure, electability is my primary concern.
sentences.zh: 所以从这个角度来看，胜算当然是我首要关心的问题。

sentences.en: There's no scenario in which I'm going to go full-throatedly support a candidate that I suspect can't win.
sentences.zh: 在任何情况下，我都绝不会全力支持一个我怀疑无法获胜的候选人。

sentences.en: More what I'm saying is, I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我更想说的是，我不知道。

sentences.en: I don't know who can win, who will win.
sentences.zh: 我不知道谁能赢，谁会赢。

sentences.en: I will say I think every Democrat can win.
sentences.zh: 我要说的是我认为每个民主党人都能赢。

sentences.en: I'm not super responsive to arguments.
sentences.zh: 我不太赞同这种论点。

sentences.en: It's like, I'm backing this candidate because the rest of them won't win.
sentences.zh: 就好像是，我支持这个候选人是因为其他人赢不了。

sentences.en: I think we run the risk of over-learning the lessons of 2016.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们有过度汲取2016年教训的风险。

sentences.en: But the Obama campaign worked in 2008.
sentences.zh: 但奥巴马的竞选在2008年奏效了。

sentences.en: Because what Iowans were feeling was also what Democrats across the country were feeling.
sentences.zh: 因为爱荷华州人的感受也是全国各地民主党人的感受。

sentences.en: And also what the general electorate was feeling.
sentences.zh: 同时也是广大选民的感受。

sentences.en: It is unclear that any Democrat in this race has the ability to recreate the coalitions which led him to the presidency.
sentences.zh: 目前尚不清楚这场竞选中的任何民主党人是否具备重塑当年将他推上总统宝座的那些联盟的能力。

sentences.en: And in that view, there's a risk of under-learning lessons from 2016.
sentences.zh: 从这个角度来看，则存在未能充分吸取2016年教训的风险。

sentences.zh: 如果你能听到我说话，拍手一次。

sentences.en: If you can hear me, clap twice.
sentences.zh: 如果你能听到我说话，拍手两次。

sentences.zh: 所以在党团会议之夜，我们都讨论过了。

sentences.zh: 我们会早点到场。

sentences.en: We're going to help out as much as we can.
sentences.zh: 我们会尽我们所能提供帮助。

sentences.en: And everyone's going to wear their buttons.
sentences.zh: 每个人都会佩戴他们的徽章。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 好。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.zh: 行吧。

sentences.zh: 还有最后的问题吗？

sentences.en: Otherwise, I'm going to let you guys dismiss.
sentences.zh: 如果没有的话，我就让大家解散了。

sentences.zh: 行了。

sentences.zh: 谢谢。
